sentences.text:
09.05.2025 Heard Mr. J. Kalita, learned counsel for the petitioner; Mr. D. Gogoi, learned Standing Counsel, NHIDCL for the respondent nos. 1 & 2; Ms. N. Bordoloi, learned Standing Counsel,
Revenue Department for the respondent no. 3; and Mr. S. Roy, learned State Counsel for the respondent nos. 4 & 5.

The case of the petitioner is that a parcel of land measuring 189.404 Bighas belonging to it have been acquired by the Government of India in the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways [MoRT&H] pursuant to a Notification dated 02.02.2024 issued under Section 3A[1] of the National Highways Act, 1956 ['the N.H. Act', for short].

The further case of the petitioner is that the compensation amount under Section 3G of the N.H. Act has been assessed at Rs. 9,68,52,964/-
against the acquired land.
Mr. Kalita, learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that at the time of preferring the writ petition, the petitioner was disbursed a sum of Rs. 5,43,88,432/-.

Mr. Kalita has submitted that he has received instruction in the meantime that another sum of Rs. 2,17,12,103/- has been disbursed to the petitioner, meaning thereby, a sum of Rs. 2,07,52,429/- has remained to be disbursed out of the amount assessed under Section 3G of the N.H. Act till date.

As Mr. Gogoi, learned Standing Counsel, NHIDCL has appeared and accepted notices on behalf of the respondent nos. 1 & 2; Ms. N. Bordoloi, learned Standing Counsel, Revenue Page No.# 3/3 Department has appeared and accepted notice on behalf of the respondent no. 3; and Mr. Roy,
learned State Counsel has appeared and accepted notices on behalf of the respondent nos. 4 & 5,

Mr. Roy, learned State Counsel is to obtain instruction from the respondent no. 5 who is the Competent Authority Land Acquisition [CALA] appointed under Section 3[a] of the N.H. Act, as regards the status of disbursement of the remaining amount of Rs. 2,07,52,429/- to the petitioner by the next date of listing.
